Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

enmity noun

also hostility, feud, ill will, bad blood

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.21: inimīcitia īra ulcīscendī tempus observāns (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 2.18.2 (Lewis & Short)

inimīcitia, inimīcitiae f.

noun, first declension

enmity, hostility; usually in the plural, inimīcitiae

Examples

  • In amōre haec omnia īnsunt vitia: injūriae, suspīciōnēs, inimīcitiae, indūtiae, bellum, pāx rūrsum.

    In love there are all these faults: wrongs, suspicions, quarrels, truces, war, then peace again.Ter. Eun. 59–61

  • inimīcitia īra ulcīscendī tempus observāns

    enmity is anger watching for its time to take revengeCic. Tusc. 4.21 (Lewis & Short)

See also enemy, hostile, hatred.
